## 

## **Executive Summary**

### **Objective**

For TruStage submissions that are Future Dated and in **"Submitted for Future Issuance"** status, let agents edit **effective date (the initial draft date)** and **payment method (including adding a backup method)** before the policy activates. Today agents cannot change either once the policy is submitted, so they cannot move the first draft to a date the client has funds for, and cannot add a backup payment method until the first premium clears. The only options are to cancel and rewrite the application (often with a 24-48 working-hour wait and no guaranteed reapproval), or to wait for the first premium and then change only recurring details.  
An effective-date change is not a field edit: it **re-submits the policy** through the TruStage submission path (validation, license and contracting checks, document regeneration). A payment-method or backup-method change does **not** re-submit.  
**Hypothesis:** letting agents align the first draft date with when the client has funds, and add a backup method before activation, reduces Initial Premium Failures (IPF), pre-activation cancellations, and later policy lapses.

### **Motivation**

> * Agents ask for this regularly. \[Agent Signal\] In Jul-Sep 2026, CX call summaries record about 246 calls (about 80 a month, about 0.6% of ingested CX calls) where support told the caller the effective date or payment method cannot be changed on a submitted policy;   
> * The gap reduces backup-payment adoption: agents are prompted to add a backup CC at activation, but cannot add one between transmit and first premium. 

### **Goals & Success Metrics**

**North star metrics** 

> 1. **IPF rate** on Future Dated TruStage policies (down).  
> 2. **Number of cancelled policies** (pre-activation cancellations) on Future Dated TruStage policies (down). Track the count, and report it as a rate per submitted Future Dated policy as well so volume swings do not mask the effect.

**Secondary metrics (suggested, pending PM confirmation):**

> * Cancel-and-resubmit requests (down).  
> * Backup-payment attach rate before activation (up).  
> * Edit success rate: edits applied versus edits attempted, split by effective-date and payment-method edits.

**Guardrail:** failure rate of re-submitted policies no worse than first submissions. Tracked as a key outcome, not a blocker to building.  
**Expected impact:** \[PLACEHOLDER — PM to fill after baselines are pulled, before stakeholder review. Owner: Priyanshu Bhalotia\]. Baselines for IPF and cancellations have not been pulled; see Analytics.

### **Scope & Assumptions**

**Scope:**

> * It will be for freshly started policies, policies in progress will be excluded.   
> * Edit **effective date** (initial draft date) on a policy in **"Submitted for Future Issuance"** only. The change re-submits the policy.  
> * Edit or add **payment method**, including adding a **backup** method, on the same status. No re-submission.  
> * who can edit \- writing agent only  
> * **Surface:** Customer 360 (C360) page in the agent portal; UX pending the design step.  
> * **OTP re-authorization** of every edit via same component as the existing payment update. the agent enters the code the customer supplies; expiry and retries use existing logic.  
> * **Payment Authorization form updated** when the payment method changes (latest ETH-PAYAUTH-2026). The OTP counts as the customer's signature. The updated form is stored with the application documents in the member portal. Effective-date-only edits need the OTP and form update also.  
> * **Customer confirmation** by email and SMS after a successful edit.  
> * **Eligibility rules:** status must be "Submitted for Future Issuance"; if effective\_at is **today**, no edits are allowed (neither date nor payment method).  
> * **Date picker constraints** from IPP validation: cannot cross the insured's age-nearest-birthday threshold; cannot exceed case creation date \+ 30 days; days 29, 30, 31 excluded.  
> * **Rollback safety:** original effectiveAt and first payment date stored before any change.  
> * **Carrier phasing: Phase 1 \= TruStage**, **Phase 2 \= Beacon**, **Phase 3 \= other products**. All user stories in this PRD (payment and backup edits, OTP and form, confirmation, audit, and effective-date edits with re-submission) ship in Phase 1

**Not-in-Scope:**

> * **Policy amount edits**: separate ask (needs re-issue); not committed by IPP.  
> * **READY\_FOR\_CARRIER\_TRANSMISSION (RCT)** and every other status, including "Future Dated Issuance Failed" and "Submitted \- Decision Pending". Compliance requirement. RCT payment updates need an engineer check and belong to the "policy submitted but stuck / not activated" work stream.  
> * Post-activation payment method changes (existing flows).

>   
**Key Assumptions:**

> 1. IPP can expose APIs to edit effective date and payment method on a pre-activation policy   
> 2. An effective-date change requires re-submission; policy re-issue (amount) stays out of scope.  
> 3. Re-submission after an edit does not fail at a higher rate than first submissions.  
> 4. Adding a backup payment method pre-activation is stored, never charged at the initial premium  
> 5. The client can receive an OTP and read it to the agent;   
> 6. If the date picker never crosses the age-nearest-birthday threshold, premium/coverage mismatch cannot occur on re-submission.

## **Requirements**

### **Context**

**Current State:** After an agent submits a TruStage application for a Future Dated policy, the policy shows "Submitted for Future Issuance" and the premium is collected on the scheduled date. Agents are told to ensure the client has sufficient funds. If the first payment fails the status becomes "Future Dated Issuance Failed". TruStage is one of the carriers where Ethos collects both P0 and P1+ (as of Aug 2026). Agents cannot edit the effective date or payment details of a submitted policy and cannot add a backup payment method until the first premium clears. Workarounds: cancel and resubmit, or an ops request for a manual change. Post-activation agent payment updates already use an OTP as proof of authorization with an automated customer notification.

**Status Quo Pain Points:**

> * Draft date cannot be moved to match client funds, producing avoidable IPF.  
> * Backup payment methods cannot be added in the window where agents are prompted to add them.  
> * Cancel-and-resubmit loses the original submission, forces the client through the application again, and carries a 24-48 working-hour wait with no guaranteed reapproval; the ops path is manual and slow.  
> * Waiting for the first premium and then changing recurring details does not help the first draft.

| V9 | Dependent services down | Re-submission blocked if Document Service, mi6, ts-ips, payment-service or PASS is unavailable | Fail safely before changing anything where possible; show a retry-later message; never leave a partial change. | IPP |
| V10 | No history for effectiveAt / firstPremiumDate | Simple column overwrites; old values lost after SET\_EFFECTIVE\_AT and POST /payment-dates | Edit flow stores originals before mutation and restores them (and re-submits with the old dates) if any step fails. Write an audit record of old and new values. | IPP stores |
| V11 | Stale payment-service schedule | CREATE\_PAYMENT\_SCHEDULE skips if a schedule exists; recurring invoices keep the old day-of-month | **Launch blocker.** Recurring schedule follows the new date, or the edit is not shipped. **\[Decision pending on eggg\]** (update the schedule vs recreate). | IPP, Payments |
| V12 | Number of changes | No carrier-side restriction on the number of changes, as long as the target date is within 30 days; dev: technically unconstrained | **\[Decision\]** Suggested internal cap of **1-3 changes per policy:** only committed changes count.  to be decided by Product/ Security | PM, Security |
| V13 | Payment-method / backup edits | No re-submission impact.  | Apply immediately after OTP; update the Payment Authorization form; TruStage first (Phase 1); specify TX-103 needs to be regenerated for Beacon and Sahara in Phase 2; restrict the backup option to policies that support it. | IPP, Compliance, PM |
| V14 | Re-submission failure | If a rollback fails, the system raises an engineering alert to \[IPP on-call / team TBD\] with the policy ID and the original and attempted values.  | If the commit fails after the OTP was verified, the edit is rolled back, the agent sees the specific reason, and any retry runs a new dry run and requires a new OTP. A used OTP is never reused. The policy is blocked from further edits and the agent sees “We couldn’t complete this change. Support has been notified.”  | IPP |

(The form says previous business day for Business Day and Social Security, while our payment schedule types doc says next, and says Social Security is unconfirmed.)  | Approver: Payments, Compliance. |

### **Non-Functional Requirements**

> * **Security:** every edit requires a verified OTP; only the last four digits of an account or card appear in the UI, comms and logs; full account details are never logged; edit endpoints enforce the same agent-to-policy authorization as C360.  
> * **Auditability:** record who edited, when, old and new values, and OTP verification outcome for every attempt (success or failure).  
> * **Reliability / consistency:** a date edit is all-or-nothing from the agent's perspective; a failure restores prior dates (V10). Eligibility is validated server-side at apply time.  
> * **Performance:** date edits include document regeneration and several service calls; the UI shows an in-progress state and a bounded timeout. Target latency to be set with IPP once the contract is known.  
> * **Availability:** if a dependent service is unavailable, the edit is blocked with a retry-later message and no partial change.  
> * **Scalability:** expected low volume ; no special scaling requirement.

## **Solution Overview**

### **Design / Flow Diagrams**

**Proposed edit flow (for design and IPP review):**

> 1. Agent opens the policy in C360 ("Submitted for Future Issuance", effective\_at after today).  
> 2. Agent changes the effective date, the payment method, or both.  
> 3. **Dry run** (no database changes): PRT calls IPP to validate the edit end to end (eligibility, license/appointment, date window, re-submission checks). If it fails, the agent sees the reason and no OTP is sent.  
> 4. Only after a passing dry run, PRT calls the IDV API to send an OTP to the customer; the agent enters the code the customer provides.  
> 5. PRT calls the IDV API to send an OTP to the customer; agent enters the code the customer provides.  
> 6. If the payment method changed, the Payment Authorization form is updated (OTP as signature) and stored with application documents.  
> 7. PRT calls the IPP API: payment/backup edits apply directly; an effective-date edit stores originals, updates dates and payment schedule, and re-submits the policy.  
> 8. On success, customer receives an email and SMS; on failure, originals are restored and the agent sees the reason.

### **Surfaces (payment surface enumeration)**

| Surface | In scope? | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| C360 (agent portal) | In scope | Only agent-facing surface |
| Member portal (customer) | Out of scope | Updated form is stored here; customer-facing editing is not part of this PRD |
| Pay Now / payment plan / Stripe / payment link | Not applicable | Pre-activation TruStage premium is collected by the scheduled draft |
